title: Officer had no 'reasonable options'; Police had no other avenue than to shoot: Rules inquest
article: An inquest into the shooting death of an indigenous man at the hands of Winnipeg police nine years ago has concluded the officer responsible had no other options left to him.

The report released Friday concluded Winnipeg police had exhausted all options to subdue Craig McDougall when P/Sgt. Curtis Beyak fired his weapon and killed him outside a Simcoe Street home in August 2008.

"I have concluded that the officer who shot him had no other reasonable options left to him when Craig McDougall approached him and the residents of 788 Simcoe, including a young child, brandishing a knife in a threatening manner," Judge Anne Krahn wrote in her report, noting a taser device had been used on McDougall to no avail.

Police were called to the home on Simcoe around 4:30 a.m. and McDougall emerged from the back yard with a knife. Officers told him to drop the knife and he did not. A taser was deployed and McDougall continued towards the front door where officers were, beginning to raise the knife when Beyak shot him.

In her report, Krahn also submitted 16 recommendations for the Winnipeg Police Service and the justice system to address issues from police relations with indigenous people to the length of proceedings for inquests.
Krahn ruled there wasn't sufficient evidence to suggest systemic racism was at play in McDougall's death.
